report.executive_summary: All four pump modules qualify under the policy (quality at least 80, raw defects at most 5), so reject_all is unnecessary. On the shared fixed-duty acceptance run, P2 measures 12 kWh against 52 kWh for P3, 56 kWh for P1 and 58 kWh for P4. P2 is therefore the lowest-energy qualifying package and the policy winner, leading by 40, 44 and 46 kWh respectively. P4 stands out as the only zero-defect module; whether that record outweighs its 46 kWh gap is flagged as an open weighting question for the verification stage. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified and excluded from ranking.
report.figure_caption: Figure: qualifying modules by measured kWh on the shared acceptance run, with quality and defect flags; P2 leads at 12 kWh and P4 is the sole zero-defect entry.

recommendation.rationale: P2 qualifies (quality 97, 1 defect) and posts the minimum measured energy of 12 kWh on the shared run; the policy selects the lowest-energy qualifying package, and P2's lead of 40-46 kWh over every rival is decisive. P4's zero-defect record is logged as an open secondary signal and does not alter the written outcome.

sections.body: Screening applies the trusted table verbatim. P1 (quality 84, defects 4), P2 (97, 1), P3 (80, 3) and P4 (81, 0) all meet quality at least 80 and sit at or under the 5-defect ceiling, so the whole pool qualifies. Margins differ: P4 clears the ceiling by 5 counts, P2 by 4, P3 by 2, P1 by only 1. P1 is therefore one defect from disqualification, a robustness caveat worth recording even though eligibility today is unaffected. Quality spans 80 to 97, with P2 highest and P3 exactly at the threshold.
sections.heading: 1. Eligibility Screening Against Policy

sections.body: On the shared acceptance run the ranking is P2 at 12 kWh, then P3 at 52, P1 at 56 and P4 at 58. Policy minimizes energy among qualifying candidates, so P2 leads outright and the minimum is unique, leaving no tie-break. Gap arithmetic: P3 trails P2 by 40 kWh, roughly 4.3 times the leader's run; P1 by 44 kWh, about 4.7 times; P4 by 46 kWh, about 4.8 times. Because every module serves the same fixed flow and head and shares one test basis, these gaps are genuine efficiency differences, not duty or measurement artifacts.
sections.heading: 2. Energy Ranking and Gap Arithmetic

sections.body: Quality and defects do not co-vary simply: P2 pairs the best quality (97) with one defect, while P4 pairs a mid index (81) with zero defects. The written policy treats defects only as a pass/fail ceiling and energy as the sole optimizer, so P4's zero-defect record does not change the ranking, but it is the clearest secondary signal in the table. Open questions for verification: (i) should defects carry weight beyond the ceiling, given P4 alone is defect-free; (ii) is P1's 4-defect count stable or near retest; (iii) are quality indices independently measured. Cost and reliability stay unverified.
sections.heading: 3. Defect and Quality Trade-off; Open Questions

sections.body: Recommendation: P2 on policy grounds. The checklist below structures B's independent verification and C's handover record: - Screening: recompute eligibility from the trusted table for all four modules. - Justified gaps: re-derive the 40/44/46 kWh deltas against the 12 kWh leader. - Repeat the arithmetic independently; do not copy this report's sums. - Question the open weighting issue on P4's zero-defect record. - Load basis: confirm one fixed duty and one test basis for every run. - Zero-defect P4: record its margin separately from the energy ranking.
